The animation sequences, five bytes each: the number of steps less one, the frame list ($B6B0/$B6BC, 0-5, plus 6 for the black spy from $B55A), and which across, height and depth step tables to use.
The five across step tables' addresses, low ($B660-$B673).
The across step tables' addresses, high; the tables follow.
The five height step tables' addresses, low ($B67E-$B691).
The height step tables' addresses, high; the tables follow.
The five depth step tables' addresses, low ($B69C-$B6AF).
The depth step tables' addresses, high; the tables follow.
The 12 sequences' frame lists' addresses, low ($B6C8-$B70F, six frames each).
The frame lists' addresses, high; the lists follow from $B6C8.
Low bytes of the 69 spy frames' headers ($B79A-$B9EA).
High bytes of the spy frames' headers.

The spy frames: per frame a header of width, strip count and height, then three bytes per strip (shape number, pixel shift, rows), drawn by draw_spy_shape. Frames 0-$17 stand and walk; the rest are the fight, flinch, fall, climbing and trap frames.
Low bytes of the 66 spy shapes' addresses (shape 0, the empty page $E900; 1-65 from $AB76).
High bytes of the spy shapes' addresses.
Each spy shape's width (bits 2-7: bytes less one; bits 0-1 a shift for mirroring) and rows less one, two bytes per shape.
The rows-less-one byte of each spy shape's size pair (read at $BA6D + 2 × shape).
The way each of the 66 spy shapes faces as stored: copied to $EA00 at every new game, after the shapes mirrored in the last game are turned back.
The depth or across position of each door slot's opening: $E8 and $18 for the side walls, then the back and front, the openings between floors.
The across position of the side doors (left $E7, right $19), for the computer's targets.
The computer's target depth offsets for door slots, read with the exit door.
The computer's target across offsets for each door slot.
More across offsets, read for the exit door.
The computer's target depth offsets for each door slot.
Depth offsets read for the exit door.
The four possible places for a side door along its wall.
The four possible places for a back or front door.
The random mask for each wall's furniture choice: 3, 3, 7.
The furniture placement tables' addresses for each wall, low ($BB5B, $BB6F, $BB83).
The placement tables' addresses, high; the tables follow, giving a position along the wall for each door place and random number ($FF: no room for one).

The room record's offset of the furniture count, $18. The room record layout, 41 bytes per room at $E000: four bytes for each of six door slots ($00-$17: link, place, mark and flags with the trap in the high nibble), the furniture count ($18), five bytes for each of up to three pieces ($19-$27: type, across, depth, contents, trap) and the colour byte ($28).
The offsets of the three pieces' types: $19, $1E, $23.
The offsets of the pieces' across positions.
The offsets of the pieces' depths.
The offsets of the pieces' contents (bit 7: open).
The offsets of the pieces' trap bytes.
The offset of the room's colour byte, $28.
The offsets of the six door slots' link bytes: 0, 4, 8, $0C, $10, $14.
The offset of slot 1's link byte (the right wall door): 4.
The offset of slot 2's link byte (the back wall door, the exit's slot): 8.
The offset of slot 3's link byte (the front): $0C.
The offset of slot 4's link byte: $10.
The offset of slot 5's link byte: $14.
The offsets of the door slots' place bytes.
The offset of slot 2's place byte, read for the exit door; then slots 3-5.
The offsets of the door slots' third bytes.
The offsets of the door slots' flag bytes (trap in the high nibble).
The offset of slot 2's flag byte, $0B, read when build_embassy checks the back wall.
The offsets of slots 3-5's flag bytes.
The offset of the matching door in the neighbouring room for each slot: left and right, back and front, and the two floor openings swap.
The offsets of the matching door's place byte (six), then of its third byte (six).
The offsets of the matching door's flag byte.
The depth a spy is put at on going through each kind of door.
The bread-crumb arrow for leaving by each door slot: the way back is the opposite slot.
32 colour bytes, one picked at random for each room: the low nibble is the room's background colour, bit 7 the second floor picture.
The 36 room records' addresses, low: $E000 + 41 × room.
The room records' addresses, high.
The bytes per room in a level layout: 6.
Each level's layout address, low (high at $BC69).
Each level's layout address, high.
Each level's list of map positions, low (high at $BC79).
Each level's map position list, high.
Each level's map offset from the monitor's map origin, low.
Each level's map offset, high.
Each level's room count: 6, 13, 20, 33, 35, 36, 34, 36.
Each level's map width less one.
Each level's map height less one.
Each level's chance, out of 32, that an empty piece of furniture gets an item when the items are placed: 8, 6, 4, then 2.
Each level's list of four candidate exit rooms, low ($BCC1-$BCE0).
The candidate lists' addresses, high.
The four rooms that may hold the exit, for each level in turn.
Level 4's embassy: 33 rooms of six door links.
Level 4's map positions.
Level 6's embassy: 36 rooms of six door links.
